prompt.context_jp: フロントの奥で、支配人と高橋___声をひそめて何やら話し込んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 支配人と高橋___声をひそめて…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this opening-scene description?

feedback.correct_en: This is the chapter's opening image — the manager and Takahashi are introduced as new information in the scene. が presents them as a freshly-observed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark them as a known topic already under discussion, which doesn't match a scene-setting description. も would wrongly add an 'also' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: Two people are talking. (new scene)
As for those two, they're talking. (already topical)

prompt.context_jp: 事情を知らない彼女には、その光景___ひどく気にかかってしかたがないようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その光景___ひどく気にかかって…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks what is bothering her?

feedback.correct_en: 気にかかる takes が for the thing that bothers you — a stative/emotive predicate. The scene is what weighs on her, newly introduced here.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'that scene' a contrasting topic, which clashes with the subordinate 彼女には clause already supplying the topic frame. を doesn't pair with 気にかかる.

contrast_examples.en: That bothers me.
That (as for it) doesn't bother me. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 遠藤は、これから由美にも高橋から話___あるはずだと、努めて自然な口ぶりで伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 由美にも高橋から話___あるはず…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before ある here?

feedback.correct_en: The existential ある introduces 話 as new information — 'there is a talk coming'. The pattern Xから話がある is a fixed way to announce an upcoming conversation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話は would mark the talk as an already-known topic, but it hasn't been mentioned yet. に doesn't fit existence of a 話.

contrast_examples.jp: 部長から話があります。
contrast_examples.en: There's something the manager wants to tell you.
That story — I've already heard it. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 指先で軽くカウンターを叩きながら、彼女___その瞬間を待った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___その瞬間を待った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 彼女 here?

feedback.correct_en: Endou (彼女) is the continuing topic of this narrative passage. は keeps the camera on her as she carries out successive actions (tapping, waiting).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present her as new to the scene, but she's been the viewpoint character. を can't mark the one doing the waiting.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女はその瞬間を待った。
contrast_examples.en: She waited for the moment. (continuing topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女がその瞬間を待っていたのだ。
contrast_examples.en: It was she who had been waiting. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の指先が見せた常識外れの一部始終を、磯村___ただ呆然と見送ったらしかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 磯村___ただ呆然と見送った…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Isomura here?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence comments on Isomura's reaction — she is the established topic. は frames her as 'as for Isomura, she just watched blankly'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make her a newly-identified subject in an exhaustive sense, which clashes with the already-topical direct object fronted at the start. も would add 'also', which has no antecedent.

contrast_examples.jp: 磯村はぼう然と見送った。
contrast_examples.en: Isomura watched in a daze. (topic)
It was Isomura who watched. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 支配人室に戻った奥田___、受話器を手に取り深く息を吐いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 支配人室に戻った奥田___、受話器を手に取り…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Okuda, our new viewpoint character here?

feedback.correct_en: The scene shifts to Okuda and now describes a sequence of his actions. は sets him up as the topic the next clauses will unfold around.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight him exhaustively ('it was Okuda who…'), unnatural when we simply follow his actions. に doesn't match the agent role.

contrast_examples.jp: 奥田は受話器を取った。
contrast_examples.en: Okuda picked up the receiver. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 奥田が受話器を取った。
contrast_examples.en: It was Okuda who picked up the receiver.

prompt.context_jp: 廊下の向こうから、奥田の低くはっきりした声___漏れ聞こえてきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 奥田の低くはっきりした声___漏れ聞こえてきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the voice that reaches Endou's ears?

feedback.correct_en: A sound suddenly perceived is classic new-information が — the voice emerges unexpectedly from the hallway into Endou's awareness.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly make the voice a pre-established topic. を can't mark the subject of 聞こえる (which is an intransitive 'be audible' predicate).

contrast_examples.en: A voice was heard. (newly noticed)

contrast_examples.jp: その声は聞こえなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That voice (contrast) wasn't audible.

prompt.context_jp: そう考えかけたそのとき、事務所の裏口から高橋___息を切らせて駆け込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事務所の裏口から高橋___息を切らせて駆け込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Takahashi in this sudden entrance?

feedback.correct_en: Takahashi bursts onto the scene — a dramatic new event appearing in Endou's view. が reports him as new information, matching 'そのとき〜駆け込んできた'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame him as the ongoing topic, which flattens the surprise. も would need something or someone else who also ran in.

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき高橋が駆け込んできた。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment Takahashi came rushing in. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: 高橋はいつも駆け込んでくる。
contrast_examples.en: Takahashi (as always, topic) comes rushing in.

prompt.context_jp: 軽く手を振って自動ドアの向こうへ消えていった由美の背中を、遠藤___しばらく黙って見送っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 遠藤___しばらく黙って見送っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Endou as she watches Yumi leave?

feedback.correct_en: Endou is the viewpoint character the whole chapter has followed. は keeps her as the topic while the sentence describes what she does.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce her as new or spotlight her exhaustively, out of place in reflective narration. で doesn't fit a human subject here.

contrast_examples.jp: 遠藤は黙って見送った。
contrast_examples.en: Endou watched silently. (topic/narration)

contrast_examples.jp: 遠藤が見送っていたのだ。
contrast_examples.en: It was Endou who was watching. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の中では、つい先ほど明かされた秘密も、なぜか特別な事件に___なっていないらしい。
prompt.prompt_jp: 特別な事件に___なっていないらしい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best captures the contrastive 'at least not' nuance?

feedback.correct_en: に+は on the predicate goal gives a contrastive 'at least not a special incident (even if it's something else)'. It matches Endou's surprise that Yumi isn't shaken.
feedback.incorrect_en: に+が is ungrammatical here with なる. Plain に loses the contrastive flavor the narration needs.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題にはなっていない。
contrast_examples.en: It hasn't become a problem (at least). (contrast)
It has become a problem. (plain)

prompt.context_jp: オーナーへの確認は形ばかりのもので、答え___はじめから決まっていたにすぎない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 答え___はじめから決まっていた…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 答え here?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts the formality of the call with the already-decided answer. は picks out 答え as a known element and comments on it — a classic topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the answer as fresh news, but the sentence is a reflection on something taken for granted. も would need another decided thing to pair with.

contrast_examples.en: The answer had been decided (as a known thing).
An answer got decided. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: カウンターの内側に取り残された磯村は、それとなく耳___そばだてる。
prompt.prompt_jp: それとなく耳___そばだてる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes the idiom 'prick up one's ears'?

feedback.correct_en: 耳をそばだてる is a fixed collocation — 'to strain one's ears'. The ears are the direct object being perked up, so を.
feedback.incorrect_en: 耳にそばだてる and 耳がそばだてる are not natural forms of this idiom.

contrast_examples.en: To listen carefully.
To strain one's eyes. (same を pattern)

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針___六時を回ると、由美はいつもどおりの調子で帰り支度を始めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針___六時を回ると…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the clock hands here?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜と clause, the subject typically takes が. The hands pass six as a new event triggering what follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a conditional/temporal clause would awkwardly topicalize the hands outside the scope of と. に doesn't mark the thing that moves.

contrast_examples.en: When the sun sets, …
When the child comes, …

prompt.context_jp: 数日が経ち、遠藤たちは駅前の小さな居酒屋のテーブル___囲んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 小さな居酒屋のテーブル___囲んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 囲む here?

feedback.correct_en: 囲む is transitive — 'to surround something'. The table is the direct object being surrounded by Endou's group, so を.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the izakaya as a location of action, but 囲む needs the surrounded thing as its direct object. に doesn't fit the verb's frame.

contrast_examples.en: To gather around the dining table.
To drink at an izakaya. (de = location of action)

prompt.context_jp: 翌月、テレビから流れてきた「月曜から夜ふかし」の映像___、しかし葉月美波の場面をまるごと素通りしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「月曜から夜ふかし」の映像___、しかし…素通りしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle picks up the contrast introduced by しかし?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence contrasts expectation (Minami's confident 'they'll air it') with reality. は sets the broadcast up as topic and primes the しかし contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely report new information with no contrastive setup, missing the 'however' pivot. を can't mark the subject of 素通りしていた.

contrast_examples.jp: 映像はしかし彼女を映さなかった。
contrast_examples.en: The footage, however, didn't show her. (contrast)
The footage played. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: 彼はテレビ局の番号___押し、努めて穏やかな声を作る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼はテレビ局の番号___押し、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits before 押す?

feedback.correct_en: 押す is a transitive verb and 番号 is what he's pressing. を is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 番号 the subject (as if the number itself were pressing). に would mark a destination, not what's being pressed.

contrast_examples.en: To press a button.
To dial a number.

prompt.context_jp: 十円玉が出てきた時点で 2人に話しておけば こんなことには ___なかったんですけど
prompt.prompt_jp: こんなことには ___なかったんですけど
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes 'things wouldn't have come to this'?

feedback.correct_en: こんなことになる = 'things turn out this way'. The counterfactual regret pattern is 〜ば、こんなことにはならなかった.
feedback.incorrect_en: いく/みる don't form this fixed expression. The idiom hinges on なる for 'turn into'.

contrast_examples.jp: 早く言えば、こんなことにはならなかった。
contrast_examples.en: If I'd said so sooner, it wouldn't have come to this.

contrast_examples.jp: 気をつけていれば、事故にならなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Had I been careful, it wouldn't have become an accident.

prompt.context_jp: 宇宙人に関しては 全く___持たなくて
prompt.prompt_jp: 宇宙人に関しては 全く ___ を持たなくて
prompt.prompt_en: Which noun completes '(she) wouldn't listen at all'?

feedback.correct_en: 聞く耳を持たない is a set idiom meaning 'refuse to listen / won't lend an ear'. Takahashi uses it because Yumi just won't accept the alien part.
feedback.incorrect_en: 聞く口 and 聞く手 are not Japanese idioms. The body part in this expression is always 耳.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は聞く耳を持たない。
contrast_examples.en: He won't listen to a word.
Please hear me out. (lend me your ears)

prompt.context_jp: ___打ち明けたところで、信じてもらえるとは限らないのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___打ち明けたところで、信じてもらえるとは限らない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'open up / lay it all out'?

feedback.correct_en: 腹を割る = 'to open up one's heart, speak frankly'. It pairs naturally with 打ち明ける in confession scenes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸を張る means 'to be proud'. 肩を落とす means 'to be dejected'. Neither fits 'confessing a secret openly'.

contrast_examples.en: Let's talk heart to heart.
To answer with pride.

prompt.context_jp: それでも念のため、帰り際にひと言だけ___刺しておかなければならない。
prompt.prompt_jp: ひと言だけ ___ 刺しておかなければならない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom for 'give a warning'?

feedback.correct_en: 釘を刺す = 'to drive a nail in' → metaphorically 'to warn someone firmly in advance (don't tell anyone)'. Exactly what Endou needs to do with Yumi.
feedback.incorrect_en: 針を刺す and 刀を刺す are literal, not idiomatic 'warn' expressions.

contrast_examples.jp: ナイショだよと釘を刺した。
contrast_examples.en: I warned her it was a secret.
To make doubly sure. (related nuance)

prompt.context_jp: 遠藤はあとで胸を___ことになる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 遠藤はあとで胸を___ことになる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes 'breathe a sigh of relief'?

feedback.correct_en: 胸を撫でおろす literally 'stroke the chest downward' = feel relieved after worry. Perfect for Endou's reaction when the TV threat vanishes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸を打つ = 'to be moved emotionally'. 胸を張る = 'to be proud'. Neither matches the relief context.

contrast_examples.jp: 無事と聞いて胸を撫でおろした。
contrast_examples.en: I was relieved to hear they were safe.

contrast_examples.jp: その話に胸を打たれた。
contrast_examples.en: I was moved by that story.

prompt.context_jp: 額に___汗と、うなだれた肩とが、話の結末をあらかじめ告げている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 額に___汗と、うなだれた肩…
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb describes sweat appearing on a forehead?

feedback.correct_en: 汗が浮く = sweat 'floats up' / beads on the skin. It's the standard collocation for perspiration appearing on the forehead.
feedback.incorrect_en: 降る is for rain/snow falling from above. 積もる is for things piling up (snow, dust) — neither suits beads of sweat.

contrast_examples.en: Sweat beads on his forehead.
Snow falls.

prompt.context_jp: 遠藤は驚きよりも先に、___した気持ちのほうが大きかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___した気持ちのほうが大きかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures 'feeling let down / anticlimactic'?

feedback.correct_en: 拍子抜け = the deflated feeling when something you braced for turns out to be nothing. Perfect for Endou, who steeled herself for drama that never came.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気合い is enthusiasm/pumped-up spirit — opposite nuance. 思いつき is a 'random idea', unrelated to emotional letdown.

contrast_examples.jp: 拍子抜けするほど簡単だった。
contrast_examples.en: It was anticlimactically easy.
To get fired up.

prompt.context_jp: 「分かった ここは 俺が ___するよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ここは 俺が ___するよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'I'll handle it somehow'?

feedback.correct_en: なんとかする = 'do something about it, manage it somehow'. The manager is reassuring the staff he'll fix the TV problem.
feedback.incorrect_en: どうにもする isn't an expression (どうにもならない 'nothing to be done' is). いくらする asks a price, not solve a problem.

contrast_examples.en: I'll figure something out.
There's nothing to be done.

prompt.context_jp: Okuda is on the phone declining the TV interview on behalf of the owner.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for a hotel manager politely declining an interview on the phone?

choices.text: オーナーに確認したところ、ちょっとテレビの取材はマズイということでですね、本当に申し訳ございません。
オーナーに聞いたら、テレビの取材はダメだって。ごめんね。
オーナー確認済み。取材不可。すみません。

feedback.correct_en: The story's actual line uses softening fillers (ちょっと…ということでですね) plus 申し訳ございません — the natural register for a manager apologizing to a TV producer.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual speech, inappropriate on a business call. C sounds like clipped memo-speak, not spoken Japanese to a client.

contrast_examples.jp: 確認いたしましたところ、難しいようでして…
contrast_examples.en: Having checked, it seems difficult… (business polite hedging)
They said no. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Endou warns Yumi, who is heading home, not to tell anyone about Takahashi's secret.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response from Yumi sounds most natural as a casual coworker's reassurance?

choices.text: あっ もちろんです ナイショにします じゃ お先に失礼しま～す
承知いたしました。他言せぬよう固く誓います。それでは退勤いたします。
いいよいいよ、言わんし。帰るわ。

feedback.correct_en: Yumi is a young hotel clerk talking to a slightly senior coworker — polite-ish です form plus the warm ナイショ and the standard お先に失礼します fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is over-formal, almost legalese, from a junior staffer in casual chat. C is dialect-flavored very-casual speech, inappropriate to a senior coworker.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be heading out. (standard workplace farewell)
Later. (very casual, close colleagues only)

prompt.context_jp: Endou explains why Yumi, who loves urban legends, still didn't believe Takahashi's confession.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'people enjoy urban legends purely as entertainment'?

choices.text: 都市伝説系の話も あくまで娯楽として好きなだけで
都市伝説系の話も とにかく娯楽のため好きなだけで
都市伝説系の話も なるべく娯楽として好きなだけで

feedback.correct_en: あくまで〜として = 'strictly as / purely as'. It precisely conveys 'only as entertainment, nothing more', matching Endou's point.
feedback.incorrect_en: とにかく means 'anyway/in any case' and doesn't fit the 'strictly as X' nuance. なるべく means 'as much as possible', which makes no sense modifying 娯楽として好き.

contrast_examples.jp: あくまで冗談として言った。
contrast_examples.en: I said it strictly as a joke.

contrast_examples.jp: なるべく早く来てください。
contrast_examples.en: Please come as early as possible.

prompt.context_jp: Takahashi gently calls Isomura over to tell her the secret too.
prompt.prompt_en: Which opener sounds most natural for a senior coworker gently pulling someone aside?

choices.text: 磯村さん ちょっといいかな？
磯村殿、少々お時間を頂戴できますでしょうか。
磯村！ ちょっと来い！

feedback.correct_en: ちょっといいかな is the standard, friendly way a senior colleague calls someone over — soft, familiar, workplace-appropriate.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly stiff keigo with the archaic 殿, out of place among coworkers. C is a bark that would alarm Isomura, who is already nervous.

contrast_examples.en: Got a minute? (friendly)

contrast_examples.jp: 少々お時間よろしいでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: May I have a moment? (formal, to clients)

prompt.context_jp: In the editing room, Niiza watches Minami's clip and finally delivers a verdict.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for a TV director reluctantly cutting a segment?

choices.text: ちょっと 出せないなぁ
一切放映できかねます。

feedback.correct_en: ちょっと…なぁ softens the verdict as a reluctant professional judgement muttered to the room — the natural tone of an editor making a call.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is formal written/announcement language, out of place in an editing-room conversation. C is a sharp command, inconsistent with his hesitant う～ん just before.

contrast_examples.en: Hmm, can't use this. (editor thinking aloud)
We are unable to broadcast. (formal written register)
